auditor.name: M/s Joy Mukherjee & Associates
auditor.opinion: The Auditors' Report on Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements for the financial year 2025-26 does not contain any qualification, observation, disclaimer, reservation, or adverse remark.
qualifications_or_emphasis: The Secretarial Audit Report is neither an assurance as to the future viability of the Company nor the efficacy or effectiveness with which the management has conducted the affairs of the Company.
No pending litigations impacting financial position
No long-term contracts with material foreseeable losses
No amounts required to be transferred to Investor Education and Protection Fund
No funds advanced/loaned/invested to intermediaries for ultimate beneficiaries
No funds received from any person for ultimate beneficiaries
No dividend declared or paid during the year
Accounting software has audit trail (edit log) facility operated throughout the year without tampering
The Company has not been sanctioned any working capital limit from financial institutions.

The Company has not made any investments, granted any loans or advances in the nature of loans, or provided any security to companies, firms, Limited Liability Partnerships or any other parties. However, the Company has provided corporate guarantees during the year.
Aggregate amount of corporate guarantees granted/provided during the year: ₹400.00 lakhs. Balance outstanding (gross) as at balance sheet date: ₹8,820.00 lakhs.

The Company has made a preferential allotment of 20,000,000 warrants, convertible into equity shares. Out of the aforesaid warrants, 9,800,000 warrants were converted into equity shares during the year. The funds raised have not been utilised during the year and have been kept in bank accounts pending utilisation for the purposes specified in the offer documents.
No fraud by the Company and no material fraud on the Company has been noticed or reported during the year.
The Company has not defaulted in repayment of loans or borrowings or in the payment of interest thereon to any lender.
The Company has not been declared a wilful defaulter by any bank, financial institution or government authority.
Funds raised on short-term basis have not been used during the year for long-term purposes by the Company.
The Company has not taken any funds from any entity or person on account of or to meet the obligations of its subsidiaries or associates.
The Company has not incurred cash losses during the financial year covered by our audit and the immediately preceding financial year.
There has been no resignation of the statutory auditors of the Company during the year.
The Company is not required to be registered under section 45-IA of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
The provisions of Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 relating to Corporate Social Responsibility are not applicable to the Company.
The Group has not declared or paid any dividend during the year and has not proposed final dividend for the year.

Based on our examination, which included test checks, the Group has used accounting softwares for maintaining its books of account for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 which has a feature of recording audit trail (edit log) facility and the same has operated throughout the year for all relevant transactions recorded in the software. Further, during the course of our audit we did not come across any instance of the audit trail feature being tampered with. Additionally, the audit trail, to the extent enable and operated, has been preserved by the Holding Company and its subsidiary companies incorporated in india as per the statutory requirements for record retention.
In our opinion and according to the explanations given to us, the remuneration paid by the Company to its directors during the year is in accordance with the provisions of section 197 of the Act.
key_audit_matters: Revenue Recognition - due to significance of revenue, judgment in applying Ind AS 115 for long-term production contracts and licensing arrangements, identification of performance obligations, timing of transfer of control, and allocation of transaction price

Revenue recognition - The Group derives revenue primarily from production and broadcasting of television programmes, licensing and sale of content rights, digital media services, infrastructure support services and rental income. Revenue is recognized based on the terms of customer agreements and the satisfaction of performance obligations in accordance with Ind AS 115. Determining the timing and amount of revenue to be recognized requires management to evaluate contractual terms, performance obligations and the stage of completion of services, where applicable.

outlook.statement: Looking ahead, we are poised to capitalize on renewed growth in the sector and deliver premium content to our consumers.

The Indian M&E sector is forecasted to grow at a 10% annual rate, crossing INR 3.1 trillion by 2027, driven by digital media growth, OTT adoption, gaming segment growth, and cost-effective consumer options. Digital media is poised to overtake television as the leading segment.
India's real GDP growth is projected at 7.7% in FY 2025-26, with IMF projecting 7.6% for 2025 and 6.5% for 2026 and 2027.
M&E sector expected to grow 6.8%-7.2% in FY 2026-27 driven by consumer demand, government investment in digital/broadcast infrastructure, and private spending pickup
Digital media production has positive long-term outlook supported by OTT expansion, social media video, CTV advertising, and creator-led content ecosystems
Radio operators expected to leverage automotive dominance and curated content to syndicate linear feeds onto paid audio OTT platforms
OOH segment expected to grow at 8.3% CAGR to reach INR 85 billion by 2028
Music segment expected to grow at 9% CAGR to reach INR 75 billion by 2028 with 28-30 million paid subscribers
Podcast industry poised for sustained expansion with rising listenership and content innovation
BAG plans to create and deliver popular, high-quality programming for domestic and international viewership, expecting high returns for stakeholders
Digital and AI (D&AI) will focus on viewer and customer experience, enterprise capability enhancement and cyber resilient growth

The Company intends to strengthen its digital distribution advisory vertical by expanding the advisory team with specialized expertise, developing proprietary analytics tools for placement optimization, and building strategic partnerships with technology platforms for data-driven recommendations.

The Indian media and entertainment industry is undergoing a transformative phase with digital media leading growth; traditional segments like television and print continue to hold significant value; film and music industries are leveraging digital platforms; live events are rebounding with hybrid formats; overall industry set for continued growth driven by technological advancements, innovative content, and evolving consumer preferences.
